title: Maven shared build cache corrupts across worktrees
description:
When multiple worktrees run `make build` (mvn install package -DskipTests), they share the same ~/.m2 local repository. If worktree A installs mage-common with a different CardView (e.g. adding a controllerId field) and worktree B then tries an incremental build, Maven may find the installed artifact from A but skip compilation because its own sources haven't changed — then fail because downstream modules see the wrong class version, or the packaging plugin can't find the expected jar.

Observed failure: after merging origin/master into a branch that modified CardView.java and GameView.java, `make build` failed with:

    Failed to execute goal maven-install-plugin:3.1.4:install on project mage-common:
    The packaging plugin for project mage-common did not assign a file to the build artifact

All downstream modules were SKIPPED. A `make clean && make build` fixed it, but this shouldn't happen — parallel worktrees should never corrupt each other's builds.

Investigation should cover:
1. Whether `mvn install` writing to the shared ~/.m2/repository is the root cause (worktree A's installed jar gets picked up by worktree B's incremental build)
2. Whether worktrees should use isolated local repositories (e.g. `-Dmaven.repo.local=.m2-local`) to prevent cross-contamination
3. Whether the previous decision to re-enable incremental compilation (see git history for p3-investigate-reenabling-maven-incremental-compilation) needs to be revisited
4. Whether `make build` should always do a clean install, or whether there's a lighter-weight fix

This is P2 because it causes mysterious build failures that waste Claude time and block work. The workaround is `make clean && make build` but that shouldn't be necessary.
